verdict.rationale: Supabase's official MCP server lets an agent query the database and manage migrations. That covers SQL and schema operations through first-party tools, and the hosted MCP endpoint was confirmed live. The read-only vs destructive distinction is evidenced only by a Supabase engineer's community comment about encouraging read-only MCP by default, not by first-party docs. The reported prompt-injection exploit concerns injection risk, not a failure of a read-only mode, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of read-only/destructive tool scoping, per-tool permission or confirmation controls, independent hands-on corroboration of safe delegation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can run SQL and schema operations through scoped tools that distinguish read-only from destructive actions, so I can safely delegate database work

citations.quote: so your agent can query your database, manage migrations, deploy Edge Functions
